posts.text: Our best protection from all of those risks might be using CTI software to ratify a World Constitution that is based on the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Earth Charter.

posts.author: John Kintree
posts.text: Laws are passed by elected representatives. Supreme laws are approved by referendums with direct votes by the people, whether it's at the local, state, national, or global level.

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: The International Court of Justice can rule on disputes between states, but its judgments are only enforced if the Security Council chooses to act. A court whose rulings depend on the goodwill of the parties is not a court in the ordinary sense.

solutions.name: Compulsory jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: Most states have never accepted the International Court of Justice's compulsory jurisdiction, and several that once did have since withdrawn. International law binds only those who agree to be bound.

evidence.name: International Court of Justice, declarations recognizing the jurisdiction of the Court as compulsory

posts.author: Counterpoint
posts.text: Global rules can be enforced without a world government. The Montreal Protocol phased out ozone depleting chemicals through trade measures and a funding mechanism, and nearly every country complied.

solutions.name: Treaty based enforcement with trade measures

evidence.name: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: Any one of the five permanent members can block a Security Council resolution, whatever the rest of the world thinks. Since 1946 the veto has been used hundreds of times, often to shield the member casting it or its allies.

solutions.name: Limit or abolish the Security Council veto

evidence.name: Dag Hammarskjöld Library's list of Security Council vetoes

posts.author: Counterpoint
posts.text: The General Assembly can act when the Council is blocked. The Uniting for Peace resolution of 1950 lets the Assembly recommend collective measures, and since 2022 the Assembly meets within ten days of any veto to debate it.

evidence.name: Uniting for Peace, General Assembly resolution 377 (V)
General Assembly resolution 76/262 of 2022, the veto initiative

posts.author: John Kintree
posts.text: A carbon tax approved by a global referendum would be supreme law for all nations. The referendum would specify how the carbon tax money, $1 trillion per year for instance, would be spent. If the damages caused by greenhouse gas emissions from burning fossil fuels was less than $1 trillion per year, the remainder could be spent on financing the transition to solar, wind, battery, and other technologies to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions.

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: National climate pledges under the Paris Agreement are voluntary, and the gap between what countries have promised and what the science requires has not closed. Without a body that can set and enforce a shared limit, each country has a reason to wait for the others.

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: Carbon pricing now exists in dozens of countries, but it covers only about a quarter of global emissions and most prices are far below what would be needed to meet the Paris goals. A single global price would remove the incentive to move pollution across borders.

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: No global body is directly elected. The General Assembly represents governments, not people, and a citizen of a large democracy has no more say in it than the ruler of a small dictatorship.

evidence.name: Campaign for a UN Parliamentary Assembly

posts.author: Seed
posts.text: Estonia shows that a whole country can vote, sign and govern online with a trusted digital identity. The tools for direct participation at a large scale already exist.

posts.author: John Kintree
posts.text: Who has control now? The higher, the fewer. Autonomy requires controls, rules, and laws. I would like to see the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Earth Charter ratified as supreme law for all nations.
